frequency_question: How often does the U.S. government successfully complete all mandatory bureaucratic and administrative steps to implement a major announced tariff or trade sanction within a tight 50-day implementation window?
membership_rule: Members are Executive Orders or formal tariff proclamations issued by the President requiring federal agency implementation (CBP rule changes, Harmonized Tariff Schedule modifications) within 60 days of announcement. Excluded are actions requiring primary congressional legislation.

cases.name: Liberation Day Tariffs / Universal Baseline Proclamations

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named historical instances of rapid-window tariff enactments; population is small because short-window unilateral tariff implementations are rare.
known_gaps: Excludes minor or withdrawn tariff threats that never reached the formal proclamation and instruction-drafting stage.
skeleton: Executive actions utilizing existing statutory powers (e.g., Section 232, Section 301, International Emergency Economic Powers Act) bypass notice-and-comment rulemaking, reducing procedural duration to internal agency drafting and system updates.
multiplier: 3 successful rapid-implementation tariff actions out of 3 major historical attempts using emergency trade authorities under compressed timeframes.
validity_reason: Valid through the current presidential term as administrative procedures under emergency trade statutes remain structurally unchanged.
